Pipeline stage: field-test design

Source: R/pipeline-fieldtest.R
design_field_test.Rd

Plans how new items reach test takers before they are calibrated: the number of forms, the anchor items every form shares (so the forms can be put on one scale), and the sample size per form. The unique items are spread over the forms in turn by blueprint cell, so each form covers the blueprint. A simulation then shows how well the item parameters would be recovered under the plan: responses are simulated from plausible item parameters (mirt::simdata()), the items a form does not include are set to missing, the model is fitted, and the estimates are compared with the true values.

Usage

design_field_test(
  p,
  n_forms,
  n_per_form,
  items = NULL,
  anchors = NULL,
  model = c("2PL", "Rasch", "3PL", "graded"),
  reps = 10,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

p

a pipeline.

n_forms

number of field-test forms.

n_per_form

number of test takers who take each form.

items

the items to field-test: by default the approved items in the pipeline (or every item not rejected, if none has been reviewed); or a character vector of item ids; or a number of items, for planning before items exist.

anchors

optional anchor item ids. By default the fewest items that make up min_anchor_share of a form, taken in turn from each blueprint cell.

model

the model the items will be calibrated with: "2PL", "Rasch", "3PL" or "graded" (polytomous items use the graded model in any case).

reps

number of simulated field tests (0 skips the simulation).

seed

optional random seed.

Value

The pipeline with p$field_test: forms (a tibble with one row per form and item, and its role), items (respondents per item), recovery (average RMSE of slopes and intercepts over the replications) and the settings.

Details

The checks (thresholds from mv_rules()):

  • sample_size (review): items answered by fewer than n_rasch, n_2pl or n_3pl respondents, depending on the model (polytomous items count as needing n_3pl).

  • anchor_share (review): the anchors make up less than min_anchor_share of a form.

  • anchor_coverage (review): a blueprint cell with no anchor item, so the link between forms does not represent it.

  • recovery (review): the average RMSE of the simulated slopes (or of the intercepts, for the Rasch model) is above recovery_rmse.

Examples

# \donttest{
p <- design_field_test(mv_pipeline(verbose = FALSE), n_forms = 3, n_per_form = 300,
                       items = 60, reps = 2, seed = 1)
p$field_test$items
#> # A tibble: 60 × 4
#>    item  forms     n role  
#>    <chr> <int> <dbl> <chr> 
#>  1 I001      3   900 anchor
#>  2 I002      3   900 anchor
#>  3 I003      3   900 anchor
#>  4 I004      3   900 anchor
#>  5 I005      3   900 anchor
#>  6 I006      1   300 unique
#>  7 I007      1   300 unique
#>  8 I008      1   300 unique
#>  9 I009      1   300 unique
#> 10 I010      1   300 unique
#> # ℹ 50 more rows
flags(p)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 10
#>      id stage      check       target      value rule  level advice status note
